newsitem.title: UK: DIARY - Today in Westminster - Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: DIARY - Today in Westminster - Jan 21.

text.p: The Conservative Party's uneasy truce on Europe faces a severe test on Tuesday when Eurosceptic Teresa Gorman seeks permission to introduce a bill to allow a referendum on British membership.
Gorman's bill, which will be discussed for 10 minutes at 1530 gmt, has no chance of becoming law.
But political observers will scan the division lists to see which Conservatives, even so close to a general election, are prepared to rock the boat by voting for its introduction.
Other events at Westminster on Tuesday include --
- Questions to the Health Secretary at 1430 gmt.
- Questions to the Prime Minister at 1515 gmt.

- Debate on the state of National Health Service on an opposition motion, then motions on the Selective Cull (Enforcement of Community Compensation Conditions) Regulations and the Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy Compensation Order.
- Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown makes speech to party's parliamentary candidate, 1030 gmt, Methodist Central Hall.

- Labour leader Tony Blair and Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine speak at launch of think-tank IPPR's business manifesto. Blair at 1030 gmt, Heseltine at 1130 gmt. Connaught Rooms, Great Queen St. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
